commit_reviews.summary: Cleanly separates caching into a testable CacheManager and integrates incrementally through the existing plugin BuildContext, with all callers (index.ts, dev-server.ts) updated consistently.

compounding_issues: Session 4's refactor to the plugin architecture never deleted the legacy parser.ts/generator.ts/server.ts — the final tree contains two parallel implementations (server.ts still imports parseFiles/generateSite, and tests exercise both), leaving dead code the later caching work cannot reach
ssg.config.ts defines a plugin array that is never imported or consumed by SsgEngine or the CLI — configuration exists but is bypassed by the hardcoded plugins in src/index.ts

Session 1 committed node_modules, package-lock, and compiled dist/ output into git (5157 files, ~968K insertions), and later sessions kept committing dist/ artifacts, bloating the history and blurring source vs. build output
The unrelated NestJS-like auth index.ts from the seed commit was never removed or reconciled with the SSG project, remaining as a root-level distractor

DevServerPlugin implements the Plugin interface but never uses its hooks — it exposes a serve() method called directly, so the dev server sidesteps the very plugin pipeline the refactor was meant to unify
key_decisions: Session 1: minimal two-phase pipeline (parseFiles via gray-matter+marked, then generateSite) with a small CLI — a clean foundation that set the scope
Session 2: dedicated Handlebars TemplateEngine (layouts, partials, custom page templates) wired into the generator, making theming first-class
Session 3: integrating a chokidar + WebSocket live-reload dev server into the CLI, moving from a batch builder to a development tool

Session 4: the decisive pivot to a lifecycle-hook plugin architecture (Plugin interface with onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd + SsgEngine orchestrator), which is what enabled Session 5 to slot in cross-cutting functionality
Session 5: content+template hashing incremental build cache (CacheManager) threaded through SsgEngine and the CLI as a cross-cutting performance concern — a natural capstone on the S4 architecture
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality climbs steadily and the arc is a textbook feature-growth curve. Session 1 is minimal but clean and well-scoped. Session 2 adds a real templating layer with a growing test suite. Session 3 broadens into dev-server integration. Session 4 is the high point architecturally — a genuine refactor to a plugin engine with a 705-line, 46-test suite — but it is a half-refactor: legacy files, an unused config, and a hook-less DevServerPlugin survive alongside it, so quality gains are offset by accumulating debt. Session 5 builds directly and successfully on the new engine with a 793-line incremental-build test file. Net: quality improved materially from a naive script to an extensible, cached engine, with the strongest gains at S4/S5 and a persistent hygiene debt (committed node_modules/dist, dead code, duplicate config) that never got cleaned up.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, progressively-built SSG story whose plugin-architecture refactor and incremental-caching capstone mark genuine quality gains, undercut only by a half-completed refactor that left legacy code, an unused config, and committed build artifacts as standing debt.
